item.text: {"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"During 2023, Tshisekedi maintained documented coordination structures and some implementation reach, but the evidence does not establish consistent cross-system compliance or completed milestones. He chaired the CPVS, which approved a monitoring roadmap for presidential commitments; chaired a governors’ conference intended to coordinate central and provincial governments; and convened security planning involving the FARDC, MONUSCO, the EAC force, ministries, and presidential and military officials (BATCH-0020-E014; BATCH-0006-E007; BATCH-0021-E001). The government also reported that PDL-145T works had begun across 48 territories, with additional contracts covering 731 infrastructures, and later reported more than 300–400 works ready, although these were executive reports and did not independently verify completion, quality, or compliance (BATCH-0023-E001; BATCH-0019-E009). Coordination and follow-through were materially qualified: election administration had widespread logistical and procedural failures, including delayed or unopened polling stations, extended voting, major irregularities, and limited procedural compliance (BATCH-0001-E016; BATCH-0007-E011; BATCH-0013-E008); the OHCHR/CEDAW report identified insecurity, insufficient judges, and inadequate logistical and financial resources; World Bank disbursements were paused during an institutional transition; and government formation was delayed after the election (BATCH-0011-E005; BATCH-0017-E002; BATCH-0012-R11-E001). The Joint Resilience Programme’s limited monitoring alignment and 50% full-implementation rate concern WFP, UNICEF, FAO, and other implementers and therefore cannot be treated as direct evidence of presidential coordination, though they illustrate wider implementation limits (BATCH-0002-E001; BATCH-0002-E004).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E014","BATCH-0006-E007","BATCH-0021-E001","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0019-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E016","BATCH-0007-E011","BATCH-0013-E008","BATCH-0011-E005","BATCH-0017-E002","BATCH-0012-R11-E001","BATCH-0002-E001","BATCH-0002-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence documents coordination forums, planning, and reported work initiation but provides little independent ministry-by-ministry compliance, milestone-completion, or territorial-control data.","Several positive implementation claims are official government reports without independent verification.","Some adverse institutional failures occurred under Tshisekedi’s administration but are not shown to have been personally ordered or controlled by him.","The Joint Resilience Programme evidence is not presidentially attributable and is used only as contextual qualification. ","Security coordination evidence records planning and objectives, not verified implementation or outcomes."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported implication that PDL-145T reported works demonstrated effective territorial administration, completed milestones, or compliance.","Added the omitted evidence on judicial and resource constraints, the paused World Bank programs, and delayed government formation.","Recast Joint Resilience Programme findings as non-attributable contextual evidence rather than direct evidence of Tshisekedi’s coordination.","Preserved the distinction between presidentially attributed coordination mechanisms and independently unverified execution."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
